Paper title: Multiple feedback loops through cytokinin signaling control stem cell number within the Arabidopsis shoot meristem
Gene/protein/pathway: WUSCHEL (WUS), CLAVATA1 (CLV1), CLAVATA3 (CLV3), ARR5, AHK2, AHK4, cytokinin signaling pathway
Experimental method: Confocal live imaging, qRT-PCR, computational modeling, cytokinin (BAP) treatment, genetic mutant analysis (clv1-11, clv3-2, ahk2, ahk3, ahk4)
Major finding: Cytokinin establishes a spatial domain for WUS induction through CLV-dependent and CLV-independent pathways; AHK2 and AHK4 are required for WUS up-regulation by cytokinin.
Environmental or hormonal factor: Cytokinin (6-benzylaminopurine, BAP) concentrations (e.g., 400-600  $\mu$ M threshold for WUS induction), Auxin pretreatment (for regeneration)
Limitation: High levels of exogenous cytokinin were required to disrupt spatial distribution due to suppressors like Type-A ARRs and AHP6.
Potential research gap: Future studies need to determine if cytokinin acts as a signaling cue to relay information between different SAM domains as zones change during growth.

Paper title: Shoot Apical Meristem Modeling & Cytokinin Assays
Gene/protein/pathway: CLV1, CLV3, WUS, AHK2, AHK4, ARR5
Experimental method: Confocal imaging (pWUS::DsRed, pTCS::GFP), qRT-PCR, 3D computational dome models
Major finding: Cytokinin triggers a ~40-fold induction of WUS transcription while CLV1 transcript levels decrease by ~90%; WUS represses Type-A ARRs (ARR5) to reinforce signaling.
Environmental or hormonal factor: BAP (N6-benzylaminopurine) at  $10^{-7}$  M to 1 mM; 10  $\mu$ M cycloheximide pre-treatment
Limitation: Missing data on specific epigenetic pathways or specific cell-layer dynamics.
Potential research gap: Transitions between indeterminate maintenance and organogenesis; epigenetic regulation within the CZ/OC boundary.

Paper title: From stem cell dynamics to field phenotypes: genetic and environmental factors in tomato multilocular malformation
Meristem studied: Shoot Apical Meristem (SAM) and Floral Meristem (FM)
Experimental method: QTL analysis, functional analysis (overexpression and silencing), and CRISPR/Cas9 promoter editing
Major finding: The CLV3-WUS axis acts as a central rheostat balancing stem cell renewal and differentiation; mutations in SlCLV3 or the SlWUS promoter (lc and fas loci) increase locule number by disrupting this feedback.
Environmental or hormonal factor: 6-12  $^{\circ}$ C low night temperature stress; high-temperature stress; hormonal imbalances (GA, CK, ET, ABA)
Limitation: Complex epistasis and dosage sensitivity make outcomes idiosyncratic.
Potential research gap: Mapping how environmental stressors reshape locule determination through specific epigenetic pathways like DNA methylation or histone acetylation.

Paper title: Transcriptomics Using the Enriched Arabidopsis Shoot Apex Reveals Developmental Priming Genes Involved in Plastic Plant Growth under Salt Stress Conditions
Gene/protein/pathway: CLV3-WUS feedback loop; developmental priming genes (TPX2, CYC1BAT, HIK, PAKRP1L, GGL2, UGT73B2, ENODL14, ENODL15)
Experimental method: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), Transcriptome analysis, qRT-PCR, Seedling survival assay
Major finding: Identification of 121 developmental priming genes; shoot meristem tissues possess intrinsically accumulated stress-responsive transcripts and cell division regulators providing high viability under salt stress.
Environmental or hormonal factor: 100 mM, 150 mM, 200 mM NaCl (salt stress); Auxin; Brassinosteroids
Limitation: RNA-seq using enriched shoot apices lacks the resolution of functional zone/layer-specific cell analysis.
Potential research gap: The specific biological functions of the identified 19 priming genes in regulating shoot development and stress responses in planta remain to be fully determined.

Paper title: Developmental Priming & RNA-Seq Under Salt Stress
Gene/protein/pathway: 19 priming genes (STM, ATHB13, ANT, WRKY6), CLV3-WUS
Experimental method: RNA-Seq, K-means hierarchical clustering, DEG Venn diagrams
Major finding: clv3-2 mutants exhibit enhanced salt tolerance without canonical stress gene alteration; 19 core genes pre-accumulate to enable plasticity.
Limitation: Lack of data on the role of specialized hypoxic niches in long-term salt adaptation.
Potential research gap: Mechanism of metabolic buffering in stem cells under extreme drought/osmotic challenge.

Paper title: From stem cell dynamics to field phenotypes: genetic and environmental factors in tomato multilocular malformation
Experimental method: Confocal imaging, transcriptomic analysis, and epigenetic profiling (Polycomb recruitment)
Major finding: AG terminates floral stem cell activity by recruiting Polycomb Group proteins (TFL2/LHP1) early and activating KNU at stage 6 to establish H3K27me3-mediated repression of WUS.
Environmental or hormonal factor: High-temperature stress inhibits SlCRCa and BR biosynthesis, preserving WUS activity and preventing FM termination.
Potential research gap: Specific cell-layer dynamics of epigenetic marks under fluctuating light levels.

Paper title: The G protein  $\beta$  subunit SlGB1 regulates tyramine-derived phenolamide metabolism for shoot apex growth and development in tomato
Gene/protein/pathway: SlGB1 (G $\beta$  subunit) / Phenolamide biosynthesis (THT5/8), G $\gamma$  subunits (Type-A, B, C)
Experimental method: CRISPR/Cas9 editing, transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, silencing in NahG plants
Major finding: SlGB1 loss leads to SAM lethality by releasing bHLH79 to upregulate phenolamides; Type-C G $\gamma$  knockout increases SAM size, while simultaneous Type-A/B knockout causes SAM lethality.
Environmental or hormonal factor: Salicylic acid (NahG lines used to test independence)
Limitation: Lethality in homozygous mutants limits study of adult reproductive traits; data on individual Type-A vs Type-B G $\gamma$  contributions is missing.
Potential research gap: Detailed epigenetic regulation of bHLH79-MYB10 complex; specific G $\gamma$ -G $\beta$  combinations required for metabolic homeostasis.

Gene/protein/pathway: G $\alpha$  (GPA1/CT2), G $\beta$  (AGB1/SlGB1), G $\gamma$  (GS3), FEA2, RPK2, bHLH79, MYB10
Experimental method: CRISPR editing, domain schematics analysis, phenotype branch point mapping
Major finding: G $\alpha$  (CT2) binds FEA2 to limit SAM overgrowth in maize; loss of SlGB1 in tomato leads to meristem arrest via tyramine-derived phenolamide accumulation.
Limitation: Seedling lethality in G $\beta$  mutants (SlGB1) prevents long-term SAM analysis.
Potential research gap: Non-canonical GPCR-independent G-protein activation triggers in varied abiotic contexts.

Paper title: Deciphering Genomic Longevity: Evolutionary Conservation of the Ku70/XRCC6 Repair Architecture
Experimental method: Bioinformatics (NCBI BLASTp, InterPro), Biopython sequence profiling
Major finding: Ginkgo and human Ku70 share 68.4% sequence identity; structural core domain is preserved across a billion years.
Environmental or hormonal factor: Centuries of oxidative stress and UV radiation
Limitation: Study limited to in silico comparison; lack of in vivo protein stability data across centuries.
Potential research gap: Post-translational modifications (phosphorylation/SUMOylation) of Ku70 in gymnosperms vs humans.

Paper title: The maize G $\alpha$  gene COMPACT PLANT2 functions in CLAVATA signalling to control shoot meristem size
Gene/protein/pathway: CT2 (G $\alpha$  subunit) / CLAVATA signaling (interacts with FEA2)
Experimental method: Mutant analysis (ct2-null and Q223L constitutively active point mutation)
Major finding: CT2 interacts with FEA2 (CLV2 ortholog) to regulate SAM size; loss of function causes broader SAM and robust inflorescence branching.
Limitation: Constitutively active CT2 only partially rescued the mutant phenotype.
Potential research gap: Molecular mechanism of CT2 interaction with other CLAVATA receptors besides FEA2.

Paper title: Heterotrimeric G-protein  $\alpha$  subunit (LeGPA1) confers cold stress tolerance to processing tomato plants
Major finding: LeGPA1 improves cold stress tolerance by boosting antioxidant enzyme activity.
Limitation: Missing data on the upstream sensor that activates GPA1 during cold perception.
Potential research gap: Potential for epigenetic modifications in GPA1-mediated cold acclimation.
